articleTitle: Determination of single-phase induction motor parameters through two-phase measurements
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An alternative method to determine the parameters of a single-phase induction motor is investigated. Present methods are complex and do not give accurate results. The method is based on connecting the single-phase induction motor as a two-phase machine. Calculations are then done with the two-phase measurements to compute the parameters and finally the performance of the motor. A comparison of predicted and measured performance values shows a very good correlation.

articleTitle: A theoretical comparison of some regenerative snubbers from PWM voltage source inverters
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Quite a number of protective snubbing cicuits have been proposed in the technical literature in the past. Few, or none of these have been compared to one another, making it difficult for the designer to find the one most suitable for a specific application. As opposed to commutation circuits for thyristor-based inverters, a method for objectively comparing various snubber circuits for voltage source inverters, has not yet been proposed. In this article such a method is proposed and three well known snubber circuits, which have been applied in practice, are compared objectively. From the results obtained, it is clear that some snubber circuits have better overall performance than others.

articleTitle: Insulation co-ordination of rural distribution lines
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Lightning is by far the most frequent cause of power interruptions on rural distribution lines in South Africa's Highveld. Flash density varies between five and twelve flashes per square kilometre per year [1, 2]. Eskom (South Africa's major generation and bulk transmission utility, responsible for most rural distribution) currently operates some 150 000 km of rural distribution lines (11 kV and 22 kV, woodpole construction) throughout the country.

articleTitle: Comparison of controller designs for a grinding mill circuit
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A number of control strategies are designed for an industrial rod and ball mill grinding circuit in a lead/zinc concentrator. The structure of the plant is analyzed to determine the optimal combination of single-variable and multivariable controllers required for independent control of its outputs measurements. Step test data is analyzed to derive the transfer function model for a two-by-two subsystem of the plant. Four designs are carried out for the model using Single-variable theory, Direct Nyquist Arrays, Characteristic Loci and Expert systems to control the cyclone feed density and flowrate to setpoints. The designs are compared in terms of closed loop responses and disturbance rejection.

articleTitle: Research issues in computer aided process modelling and control systems design
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The major stages of the design cycle for process control systems are discussed and the tools used at each stage are analysed. Particular emphasis is placed on the requirements of the modelling phase. A software structure for a system to implement computer aided process modelling and process control system design is proposed. This system is capable of handling the broader issues of modelling and control system design and of incorporating recent methods from the field of Artificial Intelligence. Early implementation results are presented.

articleTitle: An experimental study of new multilevel line codes
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A brief discussion of the Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) concept is given, with specific reference to the user interface (U-interface). Codes that were considered for the North American ISDN and similar new multilevel line codes that comply with strict transmission channel input restrictions are discussed briefly. A short description of the experimental set up, used to evaluate the new multilevel line codes, is given. Measured eye patterns and spectra of the new multilevel line codes are presented and compared with the line code 2B1Q, which was proposed for North American applications.

articleTitle: Experimental and simulation facility of a wind power converter, utilising an over-synchronous electronic scherbius cascade
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An experimental and simulation facility for the conversion of wind energy into electrical energy for feeding into the supply grid is studied, by using an induction generator with wound rotor and electronic rotor cascade with supply commutated inverter. An experimental setup, including a laboratory system with extensive converter controlled dc machine as simulated wind turbine, a practical wind tower system with data capture facilities and a maximal, self-adaptive power controller, is discussed. Some results on all the systems are presented, the feasibility of the system is established experimentally and problem areas are pointed out.

articleTitle: Enhanced diagnostic procedures for partial discharge measurements in rotating machines
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: It is well known that partial discharge activity is responsible for the deterioration of electrical insulation. In addition, partial discharge activity is also evidence of a degraded insulation system. Despite these facts no significant correlation has been found between partial discharge activity measured at the terminals of a rotating machine and the state of the insulation. In this paper it is proposed that the anomaly occurs because partial discharge measurements at the terminals of the machine are dominated by surface partial discharge activity in the overhang of the winding. These overhang discharges are not very damaging and mask the effects of small, but very damaging, discharges within the cell insulation in the slot area of the winding. An instrument is described which can distinguish between partial discharge activity in the slot and in the overhang. This instrument is used to make measurements on a stator where the cell insulation in the slot area has been deliberately damaged. These measurements vindicate the proposition made above.

articleTitle: 100 kHz to 1 MHz converter to generate 1 kVA to 100 kVA high intensity magnetic fields
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Power for generation of high frequency magnetic fields (in for example industrial heating applications) is usually generated using valve oscillators. During recent years high frequency devices notably MOSFET's and SIT's have found application in the 100 kHz to 1 MHz frequency band. Various circuit configurations can be used [1] with some converters such as the class E amplifier [2] being able to function in tbe low MHz range, though it seems that for power application larger than 1 kVA the series resonant converter fed by a voltage source inverter (SRV inverter) and the parallel resonant circuit fed by a current source inverter (PRI inverter) are the major contenders.

articleTitle: A gain-optimized curvilinear Yagi-Uda antenna
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Recent research has shown that curvilinear Yagi-Uda antennas are able to improve on the performance of linear Yagi-Uda antennas. This study used published tables to design a three element gain-optimized Yagi-Uda. The design was simulated numerically using NEC2, then built and measured. Both the numerical and experimental results confirmed the claims made regarding superior performance and indicate that this new type of curvilinear antenna has potentially important practical applications in communications engineering in the VHF and UHF frequency bands — typical TV frequencies.

articleTitle: Range, resolution and imaging applications of a stepped-frequency continuous wave radar
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper discusses the possibility of using a Stepped-Frequency Continuous Wave Radar to replace a Pulsed Radar or FMCW Radar in SAR or ISAR applications. Although the theory of Stepped-Frequency Continuous Wave Radar operation is well understood, few experimental results have been published. This paper outlines the construction of a Stepped-Frequency Continuous Wave Radar using laboratory test equipment and the range measurements obtained. Radar images are then produced using the SAR and ISAR signal processing methods.

articleTitle: High quality compensation of non-active power
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper deals with simultaneous compensation of all components of non-active power: reactive power, higher harmonics and an asymmetry in a three-phase network. A new control method which allows to eliminate any non-active components without any delay time is proposed. In this paper a new configuration of a compensator power circuit is also proposed. The compensation ability of the new system was verified experimentally.

articleTitle: Performance calculation for small DC motors with segmental permanent magnets
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An attempt to complete and computerize the analytical methods of performance calculation for small permanent magnet dc motors has been made. The two-segment construction of permanent magnets magnetized radially inside a machine has been considered. The leakage permeances, the coordinates of the permanent magnet operating point and the MMF of cross armature reaction have been analysed. A comparison of the computation with the test results for a small 8-W two-pole motor has been included.

articleTitle: An exploratory investigation into the state of software systems renewal in South Africa
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A broad review of software renewal as part of the overall software system life-cycle, software maintenance and software reusability is undertaken. The results of an investigation into the current state of software system renewal in South Africa are presented and the implications discussed.

articleTitle: The back propagation algorithm for information transformation and pattern sequencing
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Initial investigation into the application of neural networks in engineering reveals that the back propagation algorithm can be used for symbolic-numeric mapping and for pattern sequencing. We describe the implementation of the algorithm in a distributed realtime test-bed called ADROIT. Some major features of the system include the ability to accommodate several neural networks executing concurrently, the flexible interconnection of neural inputs and outputs and the imposition of temporal constraints through validity times.

articleTitle: Weighted gross geographic product as a predictor of X.25 customer calls
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Weighted Gross Geographic Product was successfully used to model customer calls through the South African Packet Switched Public Data Network. The number of calls made by X.25 customers was proportional to the most recent GGP figures for the region. A better fit was achieved by weighting the economic activities in the region with the gross revenue pattern derived from the major data customers. Five of the major industries of the economy were most relevant. Only one region did not conform to the overall pattern, because of the high (governmental) X.25 data usage relative to the value of finished goods and services in the region associated with the capital city.

articleTitle: Some design considerations for biconical antennas
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper discusses the use of the body of revolution moment method formulation to predict the radiation patterns of biconical antennas, and describes a novel and practical feed point arrangement for fine-tuning the antenna reflection coefficient.

articleTitle: Convergence criteria for body of revolution moment method calculation of electromagnetic backscatter from long cylinders exhibiting backscatter travelling wave lobes
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The body of revolution moment method can be used to determine the backscatter of a long, perfectly conducting cylinder with flat end-caps. The travelling wave lobes in the backscatter pattern are predicted successfully if the criteria described are satisfied.

articleTitle: The influence of the arc root in flashover models of polluted insulators with practical shapes
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A simple model for insulator flashover is developed to include the effect of the current concentration at the roots of the partial arcs that form on the insulator surface. The resistance of the conducting layer on the surface of insulators with practical shapes is derived, using a finite element approach. These resistance functions are incorporated into existing flashover models to predict leakage currents and insulator flashover.

articleTitle: An experimental study of a hybrid power filter for supply networks
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper illustrates the combination of the classic static VAr compensator and the dynamic compensator into a hybrid compensator topology. An overall control procedure for the hybrid compensator is proposed and a novel technique for the control of the dynamic compensator is also proposed and illustrated through computer simulation and experiment. Operating results of the experimental hybrid power compensator is presented.

articleTitle: A new approach to component effectivity in power electronic converters, applied to some single switch topologies
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A new set of criteria to compare rival converter topologies on a scientific basis are introduced. Power transmission effectivity of components is addressed which compares the power handling capability of components against the active power delivered by the converter. This method of rating is then applied to some single switch topologies as used in induction heating, involving a detailed modelling which includes time domain simulation, analytical modelling and experimental verification.

articleTitle: Analysis, simulation and practical evaluation of torque vector control strategies for medium power highly responsive PMSM drives
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Torque vector control strategies on two different types of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines (PMSM) are investigated, and the performance of a medium power (12 kW) highly responsive surface mount magnet PMSM is practically evaluated under dynamic operating conditions. The machine is fed by a developed oversized 30 kVA PWM current controlled voltage source inverter. The effect of saturation of the inverter at high motorspeeds on the dynamic performance of the drive is discussed and practically verified. The dynamics of the drive is simulated and compared to its performance under operating conditions.

articleTitle: The application of mapped infinite elements for the numerical solution of electromagnetic field problems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper intends to serve two purposes. Firstly, to introduce a relatively new finite element technique, just recently used for electromagnetic field calculations, the technique of mapped infinite elements for which the theoretical background will be outlined. Secondly, to justify the need for such elements by demonstrating their effect on a sophisticated test example chosen from the electrical machine's area. The paper's key feature is, that the new technique allows the solution of open-boundary field problems, yielding more accurate values of calculated field quantities compared to those obtained by truncated finite element mesh systems.

articleTitle: Specular reflection of plane waves by a planar conductor coated with lossy layers
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Plane waves propagating in a stratified medium, consisting of lossy material layers between a conducting plate and free-space, are considered. The layers may be very thin resistive sheets as a special case. The waves are in homogeneous because the planes of constant amplitude and phase do not coincide. A solution of Maxwell's equations is presented which can be used to compute the specular reflection properties of lossy stratified media in general, and flat plate microwave absorbing materials in particular. The method can easily be adapted to compute the transmissivity and reflectivity of radome materials and optical windows. Frequency, incidence angle, or polarization can be the independent variable in such analyses.

articleTitle: Object-oriented design of control system software
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Automation is currently being used to an ever increasing degree in industrial plants. However most of these applications require only a few basic control concepts repeated for each piece of equipment. There is often a fair degree of interaction between pieces of equipment in terms of safety interlocking and sequencing. Despite this each piece of software remains an autonomous entity receiving the necessary external commands and data it requires. The principles of object-oriented design are suited to the development of this type of software. This paper will consider experiences using Zortech-C++ and it's application in the control system software development arena. The purpose of this paper is to demonstrate that the principles of object-oriented design can successfully be applied in the low level language environment of the PLC.

articleTitle: Aanwending van versadigbare kapasitore as afskakelgapsers vir drywingselektroniese skakelaars
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In hierdie artikel word gekyk na die gebruik van 'n versadigbare kapasitor as 'n afskakelgapser, wat 'n aan/af-skakelende elektroniese drywingskomponent beveilig. Hierdie gapserbaan tree as hulpstroombaan op deur die lokus van die drywingskakelaar tydens die afskakeloorgang gunstiger te dwing. Alhoewel daar tot dusver uitsluitlik gebruik gemaak is van lineêre kapasitore – dit is kapasitore waarvan die kapasitansie konstant bly – word in hierdie artikel aangetoon dat die gebruik van 'n nie-lineêre kapasitor, waarvan die kapasitansie spanningsafhanklik is, groot voordele inhou, veral vanuit 'n energie-oogpunt beskou. Ná 'n inleiding oor die gebruik van gapsers by hoëfrekwensie-drywingseiektroniese energie-omvorming, word daar eerstens na die nie-lineêre kapasitor gekyk. Hierna word hierdie versadigbare kapasitor as nie-lineêre gapserelement beskou deur dit kwantitatief met die bekende lineêre kapasitor te vergelyk. Uit die ontleding blyk dit duidelik dat die nie-lineêre kapasitor as die algemene geval beskou kan word, met die lineêre kapasitor as die spesiale (onversadigde) geval. Berekende krommes wat die gestoorde energie in die kapasitor as 'n funksie van die spanning aantoon, asook die invloed van die nie-lineêre afskakelgapser op beide die afskakelverlies in die drywingskakelaar en die totale energieverlies in die stelsel weens die skakeloorgang, word getoon. 'n Eksperimentele meting is ook uitgevoer om die gesimuleerde resultate te toets. Uit al die resultate blyk dit dat kommersiële keramiese kapasitore met 'n ongekompenseerde ferroelektrikum, wat goed versadig word d.m.v. 'n relatiewe groot spanning, sowat 1/10 van die hoeveelheid energie stoor wat 'n ooreenkomste lineêre kapasitor by dieselfde eindspanning stoor. Terselfdertyd word kwantitatief aangetoon dat die nie-lineêre afskakelgapser ongeveer dieselfde gapsing vir die drywingskakelaar verskaf in vergelyking met die lineêre gapser, veral vir groter relatiewe kapasitansiewaardes. Die artikel word afgesluit met 'n kritiese beskouing van die voordele en beperkings verbonde aan bestaande nie-lineêre kapasitore vir gapsertoepassings.

articleTitle: High-efficiency solar panel converter with maximal power control
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A high-efficiency boost converter for converting the output voltage of a solar panel array, to the required dc bus voltage, feeding a battery bank and an inverter, is described. The series inclusion of this converter necessitates a high efficiency converter. This is attained by effective drive circuitry, implementing a regenerative snubber, using low loss core material and utilizing Schottky diodes. A comparative investigation between bipolar transistors, and field effect transistors as switching elements, is made towards total converter efficiency. Maximum power tracking is achieved by measurements of the output current, maximizing output power. The batteries, which serve as an energy storage are expensive and therefore necessitates charging and discharging protection. This is achieved by limiting the maximum allowable charge current to a value which depends on the battery state of charge.

Author Keywords: Power electronics in generation and transmission

articleTitle: A simple system executive for distributed real-time computing research
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In real-time systems, computer programs must respond to external asynchronous events in an appropriate and timely manner. Real-time programming addresses the design and development of these programs. Our research into distributed real-time computing has identified a need for a personal computer-based real-time system executive to facilitate the simulation of distributed realtime processes. This paper describes our initial work towards building such a small and extensible non-preemptive system executive. We also discuss the philosophy behind the design and implementation of the system executive. The approach taken is to extend the C language to support concurrency while maintaining a high degree of portability. The library of C functions which support the system executive is described. An example is used to illustrate some of the fundamental concepts of real-time concurrent programming.

articleTitle: Transistor inverter optimisation employing self oscillation for low cost and simplicity
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The increasing application of high frequency transistor inverters in dc to dc and dc to ac applications in the power range 100W to 10kW and the higher sonic and ultrasonic frequency range, especially for transformer isolated fight weight applications, necessitates a novel, inventive look at existing solutions. Practical protection, control, snubbing and base drive requirements often result in complex systems and consequent cost disadvantages. This paper takes a new look at the well-known low power solutions to the problem of dc-ac inversion using self oscillating inverters with magnetic feedback in the centre tapped topology, since these circuits are totally selfprotected, simple in concept and extremely reliable. It is shown that it is possible to extend the power range into the kilowatt region by introducing: - Simple but effective relief of bipolar transistor switching stresses. - Reduction and containment of transistor storage times at turn-off. - Effective design of transformer and effective electromagnetic layout of inverter.

articleTitle: An S-parameter model for the design of arrays of inclined strip dipoles proximity coupled to a microstrip feedline
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The single lumped-element equivalent circuit model fails for inclined strip dipoles near a microstrip feedline. A new three-port S-parameter model for the isolated inclined dipole is introduced. The new model is accurate, but simple, and is used in an iterative design procedure for linear arrays of strip dipoles which are proximity-coupled to a continuous microstrip feedline. Previously available design methods are extended by allowing the dipoles to be inclined in the plane of the substrate. This gives flexibility regarding polarization. The design procedure is accurate if mutual coupling via guided mode scattering dominates coupling via radiation and surface waves. The important case of 45° inclination angle is investigated in some detail. Arrays using dipoles parallel or perpendicular to the feedline can be designed as special cases of the method.

articleTitle: Fortran package renewal using object-centred design techniques
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The functional top-down design approach and structural deficiencies of FORTRAN are strong contributing causes to structural decay in engineering and scientific application packages. Many programs become unmaintainable after several years of user-requested developments and executional environment changes. This paper consideres how such packages may be practically and economically renewed (instead of discarded) by recovering the original design information, respecifying and reimplementing using object-centred design techniques. The approach will be described and illustrated with reference to experience acquired during the renewal of LINSIM, an electrical network (circuit) design, simulation and optimisation package and HEX, a program for analysis of PIXE X-Ray spectra. The impact of CASE tools on the design recovery stage, the need for on-hand application domain expertise and the rewards of software reuse, are all emphasized.

articleTitle: Distribution of real-time information in computer control systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Industrial computer control systems are analyzed in order to develop a theory which describes the distributed control of real-time dynamic systems. Simplifying assumptions are identified and justified, and the principles of data ownership in real-time distributed control systems are examined. Assumptions which may be valid in specific practical implementations are ignored. The resulting theory describes the unique properties and requirements of industrial computer control systems with respect to the representation and communication of information. It is used to develop a conceptual framework which facilitates the development of software for real-time distributed computer control. Methods which support reliability and maintainability enhancement are proposed, and recommendations regarding real-time response and software engineering are made.

articleTitle: Additional sound channels on PAL television transmissions
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes work performed for an Electronic Engineering final year undergraduate project. Several different systems were investigated for the incorporation of additional sound channels on a PAL television transmission system. The pilot tone system similar to that employed in FM stereo radio was found to be the most suitable and a prototype system providing two additional audio channels was designed and constructed. The proposed system is fully compatible with existing TV transmissions, whilst ensuring sound quality equal to that of the existing audio channel. The prototype was tested on a commercial television set where signal-to-noise ratios, total harmonic distortion and crosstalk were measured.
